analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers three laws of motion with inertia, the relation between force mass and acceleration, and action and reaction, including momentum definition, change in momentum over time for constant mass, and examples involving airplanes, thrust, lift and falling motion.

overview.headline: How unbalanced force, mass and motion relate in three laws

keyPoints.point: An object in motion remains at constant speed in a straight line unless an unbalanced force acts to change its state.
keyPoints.quote: an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

keyPoints.point: Acceleration depends on mass and amount of force applied to an object.
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyPoints.point: When one object exerts a force the second object exerts an equal and opposite force in reaction.
keyPoints.quote: Whenever one object exerts a force on another object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite on the first.

keyPoints.point: Inertia is the tendency to resist changes in state of motion.
keyPoints.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: tendency to resist changes in state of motion until an external force acts
keyTerms.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: rate of change of velocity that depends on mass and applied force
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyTerms.gloss: mass times velocity describing amount of motion carried by an object
keyTerms.quote: Momentum is defined to be the mass m of an object times its velocity V.

keyTerms.gloss: external force that changes motion from constant speed and straight line
keyTerms.quote: an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Hands on exploration shows how applied force and object mass determine acceleration in one dimension for constant mass.
Stepwise derivation follows the page order from change in momentum over time to the familiar mass times acceleration form.
